questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Paul was / bited by a dog / when he / was a child.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'bited by a dog'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **erroneous part **of the sentence is ***bited by a dog. ***
 
• The sentence explains how the subject (Paul) was bit by a dog as a child. 
 
• The action performed by the dog is explained by the ***verb bite ***which means (of a person or animal) use the teeth to cut into or through something.
 
• Since the action occurred in the past, the ***past participle form bitten should be used. ***
 
• **Bited **is an incorrect word as *the verb bite cannot be conjugated to form bited.** ***__
 
• Thus, the error lies in the part **bited by a dog, **which makes **option 1 **the correct answer. 

***Correct sentence - ****Paul was / **bitten by a dog** / when he / was a child.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain a grammatical error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

They ordered the whole area / to be disinfected / on the earliest.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'on the earliest'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The erroneous part of the given sentence is '**on the earliest'**.
 
• **On **is a preposition of time used with dates and named days of the week.
 
• **Earliest **implies an end point of time. Hence, the **preposition 'on' **cannot be used with it. 
 
• The correct preposition to be used here is '**at'. **
 
• **'At the earliest'** is a phrase that is** used to indicate the earliest possible time when something will happen or be done.**
 
 
• For Example - The job will not be finished until next year **at the earliest.**
 
 
 
• Thus, **option 4** is the correct answer. 

***Correct sentence - ****They ordered, "the whole area / to be disinfected / **at the earliest"__.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**The prepositions of time - **

 
• **“At” **is used in reference to specific times on the clock or points of time in the day. - *The train arrives at 3:30.*
 
• 
 **“In”** usually refers to period of time. - *I was born in 1986.*
 
 
• 
 **“On”** is used with dates and named days of the week. - *She's working on Monday.*
 
 
• 
 **"By"** is used specifically with an end point of time and it means no later than. - *The show should be finished by 9pm.*

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

Rishabh was declared fit to play the next match.

options.text: Rishabh declared them fit to play the next match.
They had declared Rishabh fit to play the next match.
They will declare Rishabh fit to play the next match.
They declared Rishabh fit to play the next match.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'They declared Rishabh fit to play the next match.'**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **passive voice.** As per the question we have to change it into** active voice.**
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• **Subject (objective case) + was + past participle + by Object (subjective case) (Passive voice) + adjunct**
 
• **Subject + past participle + Object (Active voice) + adjunct**
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *A large house was built by her.(Passive voice)*
 
• *She built a large house. (Active voice)*
 
 
 
• The **subject **of the given sentence is ‘Rishabh’.
 
• The object of the given subject is ‘they’.
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• **"was declared"** will be changed to "**declared"**.
 
• **Adjunct **is a word or phrase that constitutes an optional element or is considered of secondary importance in a sentence
 
 
• In the given sentence, *to play the next match. *is the **adjunct. **
 
 
 
• Correct sentence - **They declared Rishabh fit to play the next match.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• We do not use an object in the passive sentences wherein in active sentences the subject is unknown or is not required to be written i.e. it is understood from the very sentence like someone, somebody, nobody, people etc.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.

You and I / have submitted / your work / on time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'your work'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The erroneous part of the given sentence is **'your work'**.
 
• **You and I **implies that the work was a group effort. 
 
• **Your is the possessive form of the pronoun you. **Your is used as a second-person possessive adjective. This means that the word your is always followed by a noun which belongs to or is associated with you.
 
• But the sentence implies that the work does not belong to a single person. 
 
• Hence, the error lies in using the possessive determiner your before work. 
 
• So, option 3 is the correct answer. 

***Correct sentence - ****You and I / have submitted / **our work** / on time. "or" You and I / have submitted / the work / on time.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

__Whom was the person__ that you wanted me to contact there?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Who is the person'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are two errors in the underlined part of the given sentence. 
 
• **Error 1**__
 __
 
• **Whom **is an **objective pronoun.** **Whom** is always working as an object in a sentence.
 
• When an **interrogative sentence, **can be answered with an **objective pronoun (him, her, or them),** we can use **whom or whomever.**
 
 
• **​Example - ***Q: Whom did he tell? A: He told her. [The answer is in the objective case: “her” is the object of the verb “told.”]*
 
 
 
• But in the given sentence this rule does not apply. 
 
• The given interrogative sentence **can be answered with a subject pronoun (he, she, it, or they)**, so we need to use **who or whoever.**
 
 
 
• **Error 2__**
 __
 
• **​Was **is used with the past tense, but the question is being asked in the present tense. 
 
• So, **was should be replaced with is. **
 
 
 
• From the above explanation, we get that the underlined part in the given sentence should be replaced with **Who is the person.**

***Correct sentence -**** **Who is the person__** that you wanted me to contact there?*

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. The British were exploiting the indigo farmers in the area.

B. He lived in the district until the exploitation of the farmers was successfully stopped.

C. Gandhiji’s Satyagraha for India’s Independence began with the famous ‘Champaran movement’ in Bihar.

D. So, Gandhiji visited Motihari, the district headquarters of Champaran, in 1917 to protest against the British.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'CADB'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some __grammatical or contextual __connections between them. Also, the first sentence of a passage is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. **

__
 
• **Sentence C** is the independent sentence and introduces the topic which relates Gandhiji's Satyagraha and how it began. 
 
• So, sentence C** **is the first sentence after rearrangement and mentions the Champaran movement. 
 
• **Sentence A** describes why the movement began by pointing out how the British were exploiting the indigo farmers. So, sentence A comes in the **second** position. Hence, A follows C.__
 
• **Sentence D **which explains the outcome of the exploitation which points towards Gandhiji visiting to protest should come after sentence A, to maintain continuity on the topic. 
 
• **Sentence B** is the concluding statement of the passage as it provides further information regarding how the exploitation was stopped. 

Thus, the correct order after rearrangement is **option 4 i.e. CADB.**

***So, the correct paragraph is : (C) Gandhiji’s Satyagraha for India’s Independence began with the famous ‘Champaran movement’ in Bihar. (A) The British were exploiting the indigo farmers in the area. (D) So, Gandhiji visited Motihari, the district headquarters of Champaran, in 1917 to protest against the British. (B) He lived in the district until the exploitation of the farmers was successfully stopped.***

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Mother said to her, “I expected a better result from you.”

options.text: Mother told her that she was expecting a better result from you.
Mother told her that she expected a better result from you.
Mother told her that she expected a better result from her.
Mother told her that she had expected a better result from her.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'****Mother told her that she had expected a better result from her.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is an **assertive sentence.**
 
• While** changing the narration of an assertive sentence,** we need to follow steps - 
 
 
• The **reporting verb said** changes to **told. **( This is because we use told when we normally say who is spoken to which in this case is **me.** In other assertive sentences which does not have a direct personal object, the reporting verb said remains unchanged.)
 
• The **conjunction 'that'** is used in place of commas and inverted commas. 
 
• Both the **first person I **and the **second person you **in the direct speech should be changed to **third person she **and **her **respectively.
 
• The **simple past tense verb expected **is changed to **past perfect tense had expected. **
 
 
 
• Eventually, we will get the final sentence- Mother told her that she had expected a better result from her.
 
• Hence, **option 4 **is the correct answer.
